messages:
nightly-bot: alert -> p95 latency up on route text-gen-prod across eu-west region, triggered at 03:12 UTC :alarm_clock: 

alice: seeing the same in the dashboard, p50 okay but p95 jumped ~180ms at 03:00. SLO alert fired.

ben: I pulled the time-series and ran a quick spectral decomposition, there's a new step/shift at 03:00 on the kernel_selection latency band. noise + step pattern rather than smooth drift.

carlos: bisecting the release branch now. initial hint: PR #456 (merge abc1234) touched kernel scoring and added an additional fallback ordering.

dana: can you paste the git range? I can spin a quick canary with a revert. we should hold the rollout if confirmed. @sre-oncall please pause automated merges.

carlos: range is origin/main~10..origin/main, culprit narrowed to abc1234. The change lowered the weight for preferred_gpu_kernel from 0.7 -> 0.2 when sequence > 512. That lets the selector pick the new async-copy kernel which benchmarks faster on short seqs but regresses long sequences.

alice: repro with perf harness on a small batch of long-seq requests:
```
# harness run snippet
before: p95=210ms
after(abc1234): p95=405ms
config diff: kernel_score_weight: 0.7 -> 0.2 for seq>512
```

ben: profiling flame shows extra memcpy on async-copy path at high-kv-hit rates. KV cache pressure + new kernel ordering = longer critical-path memcpy.

sre-oncall: paused rollout and throttled queues. Creating a rollback ticket and tagging infra to reserve some dedicated capacity in case of traffic surge.

dana: i'll prepare a revert PR to restore kernel weight to 0.7 and push a 2-node canary to eu-west. asking for quick review.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued -> canary-revert-2475 (2 nodes) by dana; will post status.

carlos: leaving detailed perf traces in /shared/perf/2475000000/ — includes spectral plots, perf stat captures, and the selector decision log for the offending interval. Link: https://ci.internal/perf/2475000000

alice: once canary is up i'll run the same harness and post before/after numbers. if revert fixes p95 we can roll forward revert and then re-evaluate the scoring logic (maybe make it adaptive by sequence length + kv-hit).

ben: small suggestion: add a unit test in kernel-selector that simulates long-seq + high-kv-hit to prevent future regressions.

dana: ack. i'll open PR for the revert and the test. tagging @carlos for review.

alice: thanks, team. keeping this thread as the triage log. :white_check_mark:
